regions.region: page 1 title, abstract, introduction, and SI availability footnote
regions.finding: Article metadata and reaction-class claims were inspected. The page advertises online supporting information, but no SI file was supplied or explicitly associated, so no SI evidence was imported.

regions.region: page 1 lower-right Scheme 1
regions.finding: Generic electrophilic anti-cyclization overview with variable R groups and n; classified as a general scheme rather than a batch experiment.

regions.region: page 1 bottom-right Scheme 2
regions.finding: Two arrows are explicitly marked previous reports: I2/cyclohexane gives rac-4 and NIS/Cs2CO3 gives an (S)-(Z)-5/(R)-(E)-5 mixture. They are retained as literature examples, while the question-mark 'this report' arrow has no result and is not invented as an experiment.

unresolved: The previous-report examples omit scale, workup, purification, and some yields/times.
Generic structures are not uniquely resolved.

regions.region: page 2 left-center Table 1, reaction header, entries 1–4, and footnote a
regions.finding: Four distinct I+ source optimization experiments were retained row-by-row, including the no-Cs2CO3 footnote, times, yields, product ratios, and product-specific ee values.

regions.region: page 2 lower-left Scheme 3
regions.finding: NIS-to-phthalimide-to-naphthalene-imide reagent-design concept; classified as a general scheme, with the actual tests represented by Table 1 rows.

regions.region: page 2 upper-right Scheme 4
regions.finding: Three current-paper chirality-transfer experiments were retained separately: (Sa)-3a, (Ra)-3b, and (Ra)-3c, with their row-specific times, yields, ratios, and ee values.

regions.region: page 2 lower-right Scheme 5
regions.finding: Conceptual comparison of previous 1,2-chiral induction and the new chirality-transfer approach; classified as a general scheme, not a unique experiment.

unresolved: Table/Scheme rows omit scale, workup, purification, and measurement bases.
Complex structures and stereochemical encodings remain machine-unverified.

regions.region: page 3 upper-left Table 2 reaction header and entries 1–5
regions.finding: Five distinct cis-lactone scope experiments were retained row-by-row with shared −60 °C/8/Cs2CO3 conditions, row times, isolated yields, Z/E ratios, and ee values.

regions.region: page 3 lower-left Scheme 6 and adjacent prose
regions.finding: The multistage synthesis of (R)-3h was split at isolated products 12, 13, and (R)-3h, then the distinct iodolactonization to 5h was retained; page-6 detailed procedures were merged into the first three records.

regions.region: page 3 center-right Scheme 7 and base-effect prose
regions.finding: A distinct no-Cs2CO3 control of 3d with 8 was retained with 10 h, 81% yield, and 89:11 ratio.

regions.region: page 3 lower-right Scheme 8
regions.finding: Proposed hydrogen-bonded iodonium rationale with (E)-14/(Z)-14; classified as mechanism, not an observed batch.

unresolved: Scope/control rows omit scale and most operational details.
Proposed intermediates are not experimentally isolated.

regions.region: page 4 left-column literature comparison and conclusion
regions.finding: Prior syntheses of natural lactones are cited literature and were not converted into current-paper experiments; the conclusion adds no independent batch.

regions.region: page 4 lower-left Scheme 9
regions.finding: Two distinct two-stage current-paper routes were retained: 5d to (+)-cis-whisky lactone 15 and 5e to (+)-cis-3-methyl-4-decanolide 16. The preceding 3d/3e iodolactonizations duplicate Table 2 entries 1/2 and were merged as cross-page evidence.

regions.region: page 4 right-column Experimental Section, preparation of reagent 8
regions.finding: One three-stage preparation record was retained with potassium-imide formation, hypervalent-iodine intermediate formation, N-iodination, exact charges, 84% overall yield, and 2% imide impurity.

unresolved: Scheme 9 omits exact scale/workup and measurement bases.
The second-stage temperature in the preparation of 8 is not stated.
Table 2 and Scheme 9 disagree on the printed ee for 5e (99% versus 97%).

regions.region: page 5 upper-left Method a detailed procedure for (Ra)-3a
regions.finding: Three-stage tosylation/cyanation/hydrolysis procedure with exact quantities, operations, and 73% overall yield; used as the explicitly referenced common method for later entries.

regions.region: page 5 remaining left column, preparations of (Sa)-3a and (Ra)-3b
regions.finding: Two distinct enantiomer/substrate preparations were retained with entry-specific charges and overall yields.

regions.region: page 5 right column, preparations of (Ra)-3c, (Ra,R)-3d, (Ra,R)-3e, and beginning of (Ra,R)-3f
regions.finding: Four distinct allenoic-acid preparations were identified; the cross-page 3f procedure was merged with its continuation on page 6.

unresolved: Method a does not state atmosphere.
Several intermediate names are internally inconsistent; their structures remain label-only.

regions.region: page 6 left column, completion of (Ra,R)-3f and preparations of (Sa,S)-3f and (Sa,S)-3g
regions.finding: Three distinct Method-a preparations were retained with entry-specific charges, product masses, and overall yields; the first is a page-5/page-6 cross-page experiment.

regions.region: page 6 lower-left through upper-right, detailed preparation of (Ra,S)-12
regions.finding: Exact two-stage charges, atmosphere, temperatures, timings, workup, 64% combined yield, and 11:1 dr were merged into the Scheme-6 preparation-of-12 record.

regions.region: page 6 right column, detailed preparation of (Ra,R)-13 and hydrolysis to (R)-3h
regions.finding: The two-step 12-to-13 preparation and the distinct nitrile hydrolysis to (R)-3h were merged with their Scheme-6 records, preserving 60%/72% yields and dr values.

regions.region: page 6 lower-right, preparation of (S)-3h
regions.finding: A separate Method-a preparation of (S)-3h was retained with 27% yield, 91% purity, and 1:1 dr; characterization continues on page 7, which is outside this pass and is not claimed covered.

unresolved: The (S)-3h characterization continues beyond page 6 and was not reviewed here.
Intermediate naming inconsistencies and complex stereochemistry require expert review.
